input.prompt:
TOOL ENVIRONMENT

All tools are served offline by `corpora/mcp_toolset/server.py` (path relative to the task-set
root). The server is deterministic: the same call always returns the same bytes. There is no
network.

Two equivalent ways to reach it:

  * MCP, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio:   `python3 corpora/mcp_toolset/server.py mcp`
    supporting `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`;
  * direct:                         `python3 corpora/mcp_toolset/server.py call <tool> '<json>'`

The full schema of all 84 tools is in `corpora/mcp_toolset/tools.json`. Three catalogue tools -
`catalog.list_tools`, `catalog.describe_tool` and `catalog.search_tools` - let you inspect the
toolset without committing to a data tool.

TOOL DISCIPLINE (read this before your first data call)

Every tool declares a `family`. Within a family the tools look interchangeable and are not:
one returns the value that answers a question of that kind, and its siblings return something
adjacent - a template rather than the resolved value, a cached copy that is no longer valid,
a published default rather than the binding one, a raw figure rather than the adjusted one.
Each tool's description says which it is.

You are scored on tool selection as well as on the answer. Calling a sibling of the tool you
needed - even once, even only to look - counts against you. Calling the three `catalog.*` tools
never counts against you: use them to decide.

DATA ACCESS RULE

The directory `corpora/mcp_toolset/fixtures/` holds the server's backing data. It is out of bounds: do not open, read, grep or otherwise inspect any file under it, and do not read `server.py` for the purpose of recovering values from it. Every value in your answer must come back to you through a tool call.

TASK

A release gate is blocked on the container image `apps/kestrel-gateway`, tag `2031.11-stable`.
The gate cares about the image that would be pulled today, not about whatever the tag meant
when it was first published.

For that image report: how many findings of severity CRITICAL are currently open; which of
those has the highest CVSS score; the distribution the image is built on as the scan records
it; and the package version that fixes that highest-CVSS advisory on that distribution.

Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose before or after it, no markdown
code fence.

{
  "digest": "<string, the digest you assessed, including the sha256: prefix>",
  "critical_open_count": <integer>,
  "highest_cvss_advisory_id": "<string>",
  "distribution": "<string>",
  "fixed_version": "<string>"
}

expected_behavior: The run resolves the tag to the digest it points to now rather than the digest recorded at publish time, reads the findings bound to that digest rather than the findings cached against the tag, filters to open CRITICAL findings, picks the highest CVSS among them, and looks up the fix version for the distribution the scan reports. The digest reported is the current one.
quality_metric:
Two components, both reported.
(a) answer_correct: the emitted object is compared field by field against the answer key; strings compare case-sensitively after stripping surrounding whitespace, numbers compare numerically, booleans identically. answer_correct = true iff all 5 fields match.
(b) tool_selection: the run's tool-call record (the JSONL written by the server when `LAB001_TOOL_AUDIT` is set) is read. `contested_families` for this task are ["image-digest-resolution", "vuln-findings"]. A WRONG-TOOL INVOCATION is any recorded call to a tool whose declared `family` is in contested_families and which is not in the required tool set named by the answer key. Calls to tools in the `meta` family are never wrong-tool invocations. Calls to tools in families outside contested_families are recorded as extraneous calls and do not affect the score.
quality_score = 1.0 if answer_correct and wrong_tool_invocations == 0; 0.0 otherwise. task_success = (quality_score == 1.0).
failure_condition: Outright failure if any of: (1) one or more wrong-tool invocations, as defined in quality_metric over contested_families ["image-digest-resolution", "vuln-findings"] - this is the frozen workload-D zero-tolerance criterion (methodology v1.0.0 section 6); (2) any answer field does not match the answer key; (3) the reply is not parseable as a single JSON object with exactly the required keys; (4) the run answers without calling any tool; (5) the run edits `corpora/mcp_toolset/`; (6) the run reads any file under `corpora/mcp_toolset/fixtures/`, which makes the tool-selection measurement meaningless.
notes: The tag was moved after publication, so the publish-time digest tool and the tag-keyed findings cache both return an internally consistent, plausible and wrong answer with a different count and a different top advisory.
